text:
jess: FYI customer reported streaming responses with very slow first-byte (TTFB) but total time is normal when they switch to sync. p95/P99 for them jumped ~2x since last night.
jess: Customer: "first byte takes ~1.5s, then rest of tokens stream quickly. Non-streamed responses finish in ~1.6s total, so it's clearly initial-chunk delay."
omar: can you paste the request id + example request? which SDK / protocol (SSE/h2)?
jess: Request id: X-Req: r-0a1b2c3d4e. They use SSE over http/1.1 via our JS SDK. Minimal repro curl below:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d4e" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream --data '{"model":"gpt-mini","prompt":"hi","stream":true}'
```

jess: Attached server timing from customer: `ttfb=1500ms, total=1650ms`
sarah: that's a pretty narrow tail. can we check edge flush/heartbeat config for that tenant? last rollout toggled a padding heuristic.
eng-oncall: I saw a deploy from 1766542000 that changed stream.flush_pad_ms default from 20 -> 80 for improved coalescing. devops-bot: any deploy notes?
devops-bot: deploy rflow/edge-flush-heuristic @1766542100 by luis - changed stream.flush_pad_ms to 80ms for edge clusters eu-west-1 to reduce small-chunk spam.
omar: that would increase TTFB for most small responses. it explains the regression for SSE where client expects immediate first chunk.
customer-ops: customer is on eu-west-1 edge nodes. they flagged after 22:30 UTC.
sarah: repro steps for eng:
1) hit the SSE endpoint from eu-west-1 with small prompt ("ok").
2) capture tcp timings / packet traces or use `curl --trace-time`.
3) try forcing `stream.flush_pad_ms=0` via our debug header `X-Debug-Stream-Flush: 0` to see delta.
omar: quick check: jess, can you ask customer to run this header test? provides immediate signal if pad is cause.
jess: asked customer to run curl with `-H "X-Debug-Stream-Flush: 0"`. waiting.
eng-oncall: meanwhile I'll tail edge logs for r-0a1b2c3d4e and search for flush dispatch timestamps.
eng-oncall: logs show: `edge.receive at t0`, `edge.coalesce wait 78ms`, `edge.flush send first-chunk at t0+79ms`, then `proxy.write -> client ack at t0+1530ms`. interesting: the edge waited ~80ms then the client-side path added another ~1450ms before client saw first byte.
omar: client-side latency after flush looks like network/ISP path or client buffering. SSE over http/1.1 + some browsers will buffer until a newline. are we sending proper event framing (`\n\n`)?
sarah: our runtime sends `data: <chunk>\n\n` but coalescer may compress/transform. check chunk delimiter integrity.
jess: customer attached raw bytes: they show `data: [partial]` with no final `\n\n` for the initial flush.
omar: aha. if initial flush lacks trailing newline, some clients buffer until they see the delimiter. combined with our 80ms pad, you can get >1.5s TTFB if intermediate proxies aggregate further.
eng-oncall: temp mitigation options:
- rollback flush_pad to 20ms for eu-west-1 (fast, but may increase small-chunk costs)
- inject explicit final delimiter on first flush if chunk is non-empty (runtime change, small risk)
- fallback: return non-streamed response for this tenant via tenant override (immediate config toggle)
sarah: monitoring: create short-lived alert on tenant p95 TTFB > 800ms and link to trace id. add dashboard panel comparing flush_pad_ms setting vs p95 per-edge.
customer-ops: customer confirmed running debug header: with `X-Debug-Stream-Flush: 0` their TTFB drops to ~70ms.
jess: customer-verified.
omar: confirmed root cause = flush padding + missing delimiter causing client buffering. that's a combo failure mode (edge pad + client buffering). good repro.
eng-oncall: proposed immediate steps:
- enable tenant override to force non-stream (`stream=false`) for that tenant until hotfix (done in config, ETA 5m)
- push small runtime patch to always append `\n\n` on first flush (PR ready, need quick review, 1-2hrs)
- rollback pad to 20ms for eu-west-1 if customers affected > 3 tenants (ops decision)
sarah: I'll own alerts + rollout decision meeting. omar you + eng-oncall to ship patch. jess keep customer updated with fallback.
omar: will open PR: runtime/streaming: ensure-first-flush-delimiter, link: https://git.redwood.ai/r/streaming/1234
eng-oncall: PR merged and canary build on edge cluster in 30m. will monitor TTFB for that tenant.
jess: customer applied fallback now and reports normal UX. they appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
sarah: postmortem notes once resolved: include root cause (flush_pad change + delimiter behavior), timeline, and a test in our e2e suite to assert initial flush framing for SSE/h2.
jess: thanks team, closing once canary verifies p95 back to baseline.
